name: Vicksburg National Military Park
author: parks-page-legacy
summary: Vicksburg National Military Park in Vicksburg, Mississippi, preserves the site of the decisive Civil War campaign and 47-day siege that gave the Union control of the Mississippi River. After months of failed approaches, General Ulysses S. Grant executed a brilliant campaign in the spring of 1863, crossing the river south of Vicksburg, winning five battles in 17 days, and laying siege to the city's defenses. The Confederate garrison surrendered on July 4, 1863 — one day after the Union victory at Gettysburg — and President Abraham Lincoln declared that "The Father of Waters again goes unvexed to the sea." The park, established in 1899, contains over 1,340 monuments, markers, and plaques; a restored Union gunboat (the USS Cairo); and the Vicksburg National Cemetery with over 17,000 Union graves.
